title: Fugue in A major
blurb: Ten entries, no stretto, no inversion, no recurring countersubject — about as plainly as Bach ever set a fugue out. What moves instead is the key, and the tonic gets only the first two bars and the last five.
card: Out of A major by bar 3 and not back until bar 25; the home key gets seven bars out of 29.
history: Nineteen notes in a bar and a third, near-continuous semiquavers, and he never bends the shape: four entries are exact, six take the standard tonal answer, none are altered. The episodes are short, the longest two and a half bars, so a statement turns up every few bars from the first to the last. Nothing overlaps at any point.

The interest is in the middle. After the exposition the fugue spends seven bars in C-sharp minor and seven in B minor, and the entries follow it out there — F-sharp, C-sharp, D — before it comes back. For the opposite case, open the A minor fugue next door: BWV 889 registers no change of key at all.

Book II was put together in Leipzig around 1739–42, nearly twenty years after Book I, out of pieces Bach had been writing over a much longer span. The main source is the London autograph in the British Library, some of it in his hand, some in Anna Magdalena's.
